title: Bittensor Daily News: November 26, 2026

updates.headline: SN7 changes its registered identity from Algo to Tensorader
updates.summary:
SN7 now identifies itself on chain as Tensorader, with the description Decentralized AI Trading Intelligence and tensorader.com as its website. The previous daily roster called this registration Algo. The current finalized snapshot confirms the new identity; the registration block remains 9,568,319. This is an identity update, not a newly registered SN7 today.

The website describes AI trading signals for BTC/USDT and XAU/USDT, performance-based miner evaluation and MetaTrader 5 integration. Its displayed examples are explicitly simulated, and the miner starting balance is virtual. Those examples do not demonstrate realized customer trading profits.

The exact block of the name-change event was not established in this targeted review. The confirmed change is the current registered identity and its published operating model.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: a verified substantive subnet identity and operating-model change meets the identity-change floor. Five is not established without exceptional network-wide consequences or demonstrated adoption.

updates.headline: SayGM releases v0.6.1 to restore fresh worker deployments
updates.summary:
SayGM released gmcli v0.6.1 on November 25 after new worker deployments failed compose-hash verification. The maintainer confirmed that Phala Cloud had begun adding a default port policy, making fresh deployments differ from the previously approved image configuration. Already-running workers were unaffected.

The fix includes the expected policy and new approved image versions on mainnet and testnet. The maintainer reports completing a fresh testnet deployment, matching the hashes and serving requests through the gateway. That is a team-verified recovery, not a deployment independently reproduced for this report.

This dated catch-up replaces the unresolved v0.6.0 deployment lead with the released fix. It is an operational compatibility repair, not a new service launch.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: a released compatibility fix restores new worker onboarding. Four would overstate maintenance as a major product launch.

updates.headline: Const takes operational leadership of SN50 Synth; profitability-based scoring is next
updates.summary:
Synth announced on November 25 that Const is assuming operational leadership of SN50, with James Ross and the existing team moving into advisory support. The announced direction is to connect the subnet's forecasts more closely to trading outcomes.

Miners would produce probabilistic price forecasts, validators would turn those forecasts into tradable probabilities, and strategies would be evaluated against the market. The proposed scoring would reward contribution to profitability rather than statistical accuracy alone. Detailed scoring is due in the coming days; the reviewed announcement does not establish that the new mechanism is already running.

Synth also announced zero owner rewards and an equal 50/50 miner-validator split, with future trading revenue directed back into the subnet. Those are announced arrangements, not an independently verified executed split or evidence of profits already distributed. The profit-allocation details remain forthcoming.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: a confirmed operational handover and specified incentive redesign materially change the subnet direction. Five is not established by a plan whose implementation and trading results remain ahead.

updates.headline: TPN brings its Gratis local-AI app to Product Hunt
updates.summary:
True Performance Network confirmed on November 25 that Gratis was live on Product Hunt, following the launch plan covered in our November 24 edition. The team invited users to test the app and provide feedback. This is the completed distribution milestone, rather than another announcement of the upcoming listing.

Gratis is presented as a way to run open-source AI models on a user's own device. Its website describes local processing and offline use after initial setup, with model recommendations based on the device. Those are the product's stated capabilities; the app was not installed or benchmarked for this report.

The listing gives SN65's product another route to users. It does not establish new revenue, verified adoption growth or an improvement in model performance.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: a completed public distribution milestone follows the previously announced plan. Four is not established by a listing without new demonstrated capability or adoption.

updates.headline: EveryFrame demonstrates video generation described as funded with TAO
updates.summary:
Const shared a short generated video on November 25 under the description TAO-to-Video, Gamma 117. In the official EveryFrame channel, he described it as created by his agent using just TAO, with the team acknowledging the demonstration.

The example puts a concrete output behind Gamma's service-credit model: credits for a subnet service can be created by burning that subnet's alpha. TAO can be used to buy that alpha; this is not the same as burning TAO itself.

The reviewed clip shows the generated result, rather than a full payment and execution walkthrough. It supports an attributed demonstration, not an independent end-to-end audit, proof of external customer revenue or a claim that all agents can already complete the same workflow without setup.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: a concrete service-output demonstration using the new credit model is a substantive product development. Five is not established by one attributed demonstration without independently verified scaled adoption.

updates.headline: Microtensor launches on SN129 with task-specific small language models
updates.summary:
Microtensor announced its move to Bittensor mainnet on November 26 after operating on testnet 576. Finalized-chain evidence places SN129 registration at block 9,588,339, at 03:35:36 UTC on November 26, which was November 25 at 10:35 PM Eastern. The active roster now extends beyond the former 128-slot limit.

The team describes narrow, task-specialized small language models for enterprise workflows. Miners fine-tune specialists, while validators test them against hidden, rotating tasks and rerun calls to verify scores.

Claims of frontier-model quality at lower cost and latency remain the team's stated goal and description, not a benchmark independently reproduced here. The launch post says operations are initializing and onboarding will expand over the coming days. Registration is confirmed; broad production adoption is not.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: a verified new mainnet subnet and defined technical offering constitute a substantive launch. Five is not established by registration and an onboarding-stage product.

ecosystem.headline: SubConnect launches a transaction-linked Bittensor Revenue Index
ecosystem.summary:
SubConnect launched the Bittensor Revenue Index on November 25, bringing buybacks, registration fees and supporting transaction links into a dashboard with hourly updates. This is a dated catch-up to a launch that preceded the previous report's cutoff.

At the November 26 13:07 UK-time snapshot reviewed here, the index displayed about $5.03 million for November under its methodology: approximately $4.43 million of buybacks and $602,149 of registration fees. The headline is not a measure of sales to outside customers.

The index separates bought-and-burned, bought-and-locked, bought-and-held and burn-without-purchase evidence. The last category is provisional and included by default. Readers need those distinctions to interpret the total. Its annualized run rate is a projection from a recent period, not realized annual revenue, and transaction links are not a complete financial audit.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Three stars: a useful new cross-subnet analytics tool with inspectable definitions. Four would overstate a dashboard launch as new network revenue or a protocol change.

ecosystem.headline: Runtime 497 is live; SDK updates protect multisig payloads across upgrades
ecosystem.summary:
Runtime 497 reached Finney on November 25, according to the official operator channel, and our November 26 finalized-chain snapshot confirms spec version 497. The 497 release is a spec-version increment over 496, rather than another set of new storage, calls or parameter changes.

The accompanying SDK 11.3.7 announcement describes safeguards for multisig submissions across runtime changes: pinning the call hash, runtime version and operation timepoint, and rejecting mismatches. Operator guidance is to refresh metadata and rebuild signing payloads that were prepared for an older runtime.

This is an operational compatibility update. It should not be confused with runtime 495's earlier mechanism-budget and Gamma-deposit changes, which were covered in yesterday's report.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Three stars: live runtime and signing compatibility changes are important operator maintenance. Four would overstate a spec bump and compatibility safeguards as a major new product capability.

ecosystem.headline: Taostats Gamma report shows spending concentrated in Lium
ecosystem.summary:
A November 26 Gamma report shared by Taostats records 103,676.71 credits minted, 75,835.53 spent and 27,841.18 outstanding at its stated snapshot. It was generated by doug, Taostats' AI assistant; these figures are attributed to that report rather than a fresh independent reconstruction of every event.

The report assigns 66,042.19 of the spent credits to SN51 Lium, about 87% of total spending. OpenRoboto, Hippius, engy and EveryFrame are among the other services with recorded spend. It lists 18 enabled subnets and activity across 12, illustrating why enablement, credit creation and spending should be shown separately.

Gamma is denominated in dollar-valued service credits, not TAO units. Recorded spending is more informative than an enabled switch, but it does not itself prove service quality, external customer revenue or successful off-chain delivery. The report's snapshot was November 26 at 2:26 PM New Zealand time, equivalent to 01:26 UTC.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Three stars: a source-attributed ledger summary makes current usage concentration intelligible. Four is not established by a snapshot report without a new product or independently demonstrated adoption milestone.
